title: C# Questions & Answers - Method Overloading
sourceFile: Method Overloading - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on method overloading in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: The process of defining two or more methods within the same class that have same name but different parameters list?
questions.explanation: Two or more methods can have same name as long as their parameters declaration and definitions are different, the methods are said to be overloaded and the process is called method overloading. Method overloading is used when methods are required to perform similar tasks using different input parameters.

questions.question: Which of these can be overloaded?
questions.explanation: Both instance methods and constructors can be overloaded by changing the parameter list (count, types, or ref/out/in). Return type alone does not distinguish overloads.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
vol is overloaded three times. vol(10) is 10*10*10 = 1000. vol(2.5f, 5) is 3.14f * 2.5f * 2.5f * 5 = 98.125. 5l is a long, so vol(5l, 4, 5) is 5*4*5 = 100. Overload resolution uses the parameter types, not the return type.

Output:

1000
98.125
100

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
add(6) is the int overload and prints 6*6*6 = 216. add(ref i) squares i in place, so i becomes 25.

questions.question: What is the process of defining a method in terms of itself, that is a method that calls itself?
questions.explanation: A method that calls itself is recursive. That is recursion, not polymorphism.
